figs.title: Strong and weak boundary conditions on a strip
figs.caption: On the long faces y = ±c the traction vanishes at every point. At the loaded end only the force and moment resultants are matched, and by Saint-Venant's principle the polynomial Airy solution holds beyond about one depth from that end.

figs.title: Stress concentration at a circular hole
figs.caption: Under remote tension σ the hoop stress at the hole edge is σ(1 − 2 cos 2θ): 3σ at the sides transverse to the load and −σ on the load axis. The concentration decays quickly, to about 1.07σ at three radii.

figs.title: Ring under diametral compression
figs.caption: Cut the ring on the symmetry planes: the redundant moment there follows from Castigliano with zero relative rotation. The moment is PR/π at the load points and PR(½ − 1/π) of opposite sense at the sides, changing sign at θ ≈ 39.5°.

figs.title: Moment-curvature to the plastic hinge
figs.caption: A rectangular section yields first at the outer fibres at M_y, then the plastic zones grow inward around an elastic core. The moment approaches M_p = 1.5 M_y as curvature grows, which is the plastic hinge.

figs.title: Two-cell section in torsion
figs.caption: Each cell carries its own constant shear flow and the shared web carries the difference q₁ − q₂. The torque equation plus equal twist rate in both cells gives two equations for the two flows.

figs.title: Post-buckling paths and imperfections
figs.caption: A stable symmetric path rises past λ = 1, while unstable symmetric and asymmetric paths fall, so an imperfect structure reaches a limit load λ_s below the bifurcation load. The knockdown follows a two-thirds power of ε for unstable symmetric and a one-half power for asymmetric.

figs.title: Beam on an elastic foundation
figs.caption: A point load on a beam resting on springs of stiffness k per length gives a deflection that decays and oscillates with wavelength 2π/β. Deflection first crosses zero at βx = 3π/4 and moment at βx = π/4.

figs.title: Southwell plot
figs.caption: For an imperfect column the added deflection grows as δ₀(P/P_cr)/(1 − P/P_cr). Plotting δ/P against δ turns the test data into a straight line whose slope is 1/P_cr.
